prompt:
Image 1 is a finished game sprite sheet of a leader whose drawing is right: keep exactly its camera (high above and behind, looking down at about 40 degrees), the direction every figure faces, every figure's pose, size and position in its cell, the 4 by 4 grid and the flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) background.
Image 2 is this leader's own approved painted portrait. Every figure of Image 1 must become the priest of the portrait, seen full length from above.

Repaint every figure of Image 1 as the priest of Image 2, the same in every cell. Keep each figure's pose, the position of its arms, legs and weapon, and its outline as close as the new kit allows. Seen from behind, they show these marks, and each one must be clearly visible at full size: (1) the wreath of ivy on the head; (2) the two long braids of auburn hair falling over the shoulders; (3) the moss-dyed green robe to the ground with its hood down on the shoulders; (4) a plain dark wool cloak hanging to the knees; (5) the tall staff of dark wood whose top forks into two short antler-like branches. Face-only details stay hidden, because the face is turned away. They carry no shield. Paint the marks in the portrait's hand: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible directional brushwork, a muted earthy palette; nothing glows. Keep the daylight of Image 1 (a high sun from the upper left, a cool fill on the lower right); do not copy the portrait's candlelight, its dark background or its framing. They wear a Grove Priest's kit instead of the hooded druid's kit of Image 1: no hood over the head (the head is bare under their wreath, and any hood lies down on the shoulders), their own robe to the ground and clasp as the portrait shows them, and the staff named in the marks above, held where Image 1 holds its staff.

Facing, again: every figure faces exactly as in Image 1, away from us toward the upper right, the hit and falling figures included: we see the back, the shoulders and the back of the head or headgear, and we never see the face; only the two fleeing figures turn toward us.

The last attempt failed: the figures were drawn from another camera, turned side-on and larger, instead of seen from high above and behind exactly as in Image 1. Keep every figure exactly where, how large and facing which way Image 1 has it. Keep the robe to the ground as in Image 1, so every figure keeps the outline of Image 1.

Background: one flat pure magenta (#FF00FF) colour fills the whole image with no gradient, texture, floor or shadow; no magenta, pink or purple anywhere on the figures. Never: text, labels, grid lines, borders, a floor, cast shadows, blood, extra people, cropped or overlapping figures.
